I am 69 years old and have been farming these 18 mu in Quzhou for 15 years. My household has five people, but my son and daughter-in-law work in the city factory, so it is mainly my wife and me handling the day-to-day fieldwork, with my grandson helping during school breaks. Given my age and limited labor at home, I rely on the wheat-maize double-cropping system for the bulk of my land because it is highly mechanized and gives me stable grain income plus government subsidies. I will plant 12 mu with an improved winter wheat variety in October, irrigating it three times—overwintering, jointing, and grain filling—and applying moderate fertilizer. Right after wheat harvest in early June, I will sow hybrid summer maize using no-tillage to save time and labor, irrigating it twice during the summer. For cash income, I keep 3 mu of cotton and 3 mu of chili. Cotton prices have been decent, and the hybrid Bt cotton I use cuts down on bollworm spraying, though it still needs careful management and deep ploughing. Chili is very profitable but labor-intensive for picking, so 3 mu is all my wife and I can manage; it needs more frequent watering and heavy potassium for the fruit. I have a well, but groundwater is not infinite, so I watch my irrigation costs closely and follow the county extension recommendations on fertilizer rates.
